scenes.title: Two loose tiles
scenes.narration: Two square tiles have sides of three centimetres. Trace one tile with your finger. Four sides make twelve centimetres. Now slide the other tile up to it. Where did the two touching edges go?

scenes.title: Walk the new outline
scenes.narration: The two squares form a rectangle six centimetres long and three wide. Its outline measures eighteen centimetres. The separate perimeters added to twenty-four. Both copies of the three-centimetre seam disappeared. That explains the missing six.

scenes.title: A tab on a card
scenes.narration: Start with an eight-by-five card. Attach a three-by-two tab along its three-centimetre side, halfway along the top. Predict the change in the outside perimeter before following the pencil.

scenes.title: Three new edges
scenes.narration: The old top loses three centimetres. The tab contributes a new top of three and two short sides of two. The horizontal changes cancel. The boundary grows by four, from twenty-six to thirty centimetres.

scenes.title: Read a seam backwards
scenes.narration: Two rectangles measure seven by four and five by three. They meet along one straight seam. Their combined outside perimeter is thirty centimetres. How long is the hidden seam?

scenes.title: Put the cut back
scenes.narration: The separate perimeters are twenty-two and sixteen. Their sum exceeds thirty by eight. Pull the pieces apart. Two copies of the seam appear, so the seam is four centimetres long. Joining hides two copies. Cutting reveals two. Decide which boundary your problem counts.
